        ends with a “/”, it will be assumed to be a directory, and target files
        will go within.

        Calls put\_file for each source.

    put\_file(*lpath*, *rpath*, *callback=<fsspec.callbacks.NoOpCallback object>*, *\*\*kwargs*)[¶](#gravitino.filesystem.gvfs.GravitinoVirtualFileSystem.put_file "Permalink to this definition")
    :   Copy single file to remote

    read\_block(*fn*, *offset*, *length*, *delimiter=None*)[¶](#gravitino.filesystem.gvfs.GravitinoVirtualFileSystem.read_block "Permalink to this definition")
    :   Read a block of bytes from

        Starting at `offset` of the file, read `length` bytes. If
        `delimiter` is set then we ensure that the read starts and stops at
        delimiter boundaries that follow the locations `offset` and `offset
        + length`. If `offset` is zero then we start at zero. The
        bytestring returned WILL include the end delimiter string.

        If offset+length is beyond the eof, reads to eof.

        ## Parameters[¶](#id9 "Permalink to this heading")

        fn: string
        :   Path to filename

        offset: int
        :   Byte offset to start read

        length: int
        :   Number of bytes to read. If None, read to end.

        delimiter: bytes (optional)
        :   Ensure reading starts and stops at delimiter bytestring

        ## Examples[¶](#examples "Permalink to this heading")

        ```
        >>> fs.read_block('data/file.csv', 0, 13)  
        b'Alice, 100\nBo'
        >>> fs.read_block('data/file.csv', 0, 13, delimiter=b'\n')  
        b'Alice, 100\nBob, 200\n'
        ```

        Use `length=None` to read to the end of the file.
        >>> fs.read\_block(‘data/file.csv’, 0, None, delimiter=b’n’) # doctest: +SKIP
        b’Alice, 100nBob, 200nCharlie, 300’

        ## See Also[¶](#see-also "Permalink to this heading")

        `fsspec.utils.read_block()`

    read\_bytes(*path*, *start=None*, *end=None*, *\*\*kwargs*)[¶](#gravitino.filesystem.gvfs.GravitinoVirtualFileSystem.read_bytes "Permalink to this definition")

    walk(*path*, *maxdepth=None*, *topdown=True*, *on\_error='omit'*, *\*\*kwargs*)[¶](#gravitino.filesystem.gvfs.GravitinoVirtualFileSystem.walk "Permalink to this definition")
    :   Return all files belows path

        List all files, recursing into subdirectories; output is iterator-style,
        like `os.walk()`. For a simple list of files, `find()` is available.

        When topdown is True, the caller can modify the dirnames list in-place (perhaps
        using del or slice assignment), and walk() will
        only recurse into the subdirectories whose names remain in dirnames;
        this can be used to prune the search, impose a specific order of visiting,
        or even to inform walk() about directories the caller creates or renames before
        it resumes walk() again.
        Modifying dirnames when topdown is False has no effect. (see os.walk)

        Note that the “files” outputted will include anything that is not
        a directory, such as links.

        ## Parameters[¶](#id13 "Permalink to this heading")

        path: str
        :   Root to recurse into

        maxdepth: int
        :   Maximum recursion depth. None means limitless, but not recommended
            on link-based file-systems.

        topdown: bool (True)
        :   Whether to walk the directory tree from the top downwards or from
            the bottom upwards.

        on\_error: “omit”, “raise”, a collable
        :   if omit (default), path with exception will simply be empty;
            If raise, an underlying exception will be raised;
            if callable, it will be called with a single OSError instance as argument

        kwargs: passed to `ls`

# gravitino.api.model.model.Model[¶](#gravitino-api-model-model-model "Permalink to this heading")

*class* gravitino.api.model.model.Model[¶](#gravitino.api.model.model.Model "Permalink to this definition")
:   Bases: [`Auditable`](gravitino.api.auditable.Auditable.html#gravitino.api.auditable.Auditable "gravitino.api.auditable.Auditable")

    An interface representing an ML model under a schema Namespace. A model is a metadata
    object that represents the model artifact in ML. Users can register a model object in Gravitino
    to manage the model metadata. The typical use case is to manage the model in ML lifecycle with a
    unified way in Gravitino, and access the model artifact with a unified identifier. Also, with
    the model registered in Gravitino, users can govern the model with Gravitino’s unified audit,
    tag, and role management.

    The difference of Model and tabular data is that the model is schema-free, and the main
    property of the model is the model artifact URL. The difference compared to the fileset is that
    the model is versioned, and the model object contains the version information.

    \_\_init\_\_()[¶](#gravitino.api.model.model.Model.__init__ "Permalink to this definition")

    Methods

# gravitino.filesystem.gvfs\_base\_operations.BaseGVFSOperations[¶](#gravitino-filesystem-gvfs-base-operations-basegvfsoperations "Permalink to this heading")

*class* gravitino.filesystem.gvfs\_base\_operations.BaseGVFSOperations(*server\_uri: str | None = None*, *metalake\_name: str | None = None*, *options: Dict | None = None*, *\*\*kwargs*)[¶](#gravitino.filesystem.gvfs_base_operations.BaseGVFSOperations "Permalink to this definition")
:   Bases: `ABC`

    Abstract base class for Gravitino Virtual File System operations.

    This class provides the core functionality for interacting with the Gravitino Virtual File
    System, including operations for file manipulation, directory management, and credential
    handling. It handles the mapping between virtual paths in the Gravitino namespace and actual file
    paths in underlying storage systems.

    Implementations of this class should provide the specific behaviors for each file system
    operation.

*class* gravitino.api.metadata\_object.MetadataObject[¶](#gravitino.api.metadata_object.MetadataObject "Permalink to this definition")
:   Bases: `ABC`

    The MetadataObject is the basic unit of the Gravitino system. It
    represents the metadata object in the Apache Gravitino system. The object
    can be a metalake, catalog, schema, table, topic, etc.

    \_\_init\_\_()[¶](#gravitino.api.metadata_object.MetadataObject.__init__ "Permalink to this definition")

    Methods

    |  |  |
    | --- | --- |
    | [`__init__`](#gravitino.api.metadata_object.MetadataObject.__init__ "gravitino.api.metadata_object.MetadataObject.__init__")() |  |
    | [`full_name`](#gravitino.api.metadata_object.MetadataObject.full_name "gravitino.api.metadata_object.MetadataObject.full_name")() | The full name of the object. |
    | [`name`](#gravitino.api.metadata_object.MetadataObject.name "gravitino.api.metadata_object.MetadataObject.name")() | The name of the object. |
    | [`parent`](#gravitino.api.metadata_object.MetadataObject.parent "gravitino.api.metadata_object.MetadataObject.parent")() | The parent full name of the object. |
    | [`type`](#gravitino.api.metadata_object.MetadataObject.type "gravitino.api.metadata_object.MetadataObject.type")() | The type of the object. |

    *class* Type(*value*)[¶](#gravitino.api.metadata_object.MetadataObject.Type "Permalink to this definition")
    :   Bases: `Enum`

        The type of object in the Gravitino system. Every type will map one
        kind of the entity of the underlying system.

        CATALOG *= 'catalog'*[¶](#gravitino.api.metadata_object.MetadataObject.Type.CATALOG "Permalink to this definition")
        :   A catalog is a collection of metadata from a specific metadata source,
            like Apache Hive catalog, Apache Iceberg catalog, JDBC catalog, etc.

        COLUMN *= 'column'*[¶](#gravitino.api.metadata_object.MetadataObject.Type.COLUMN "Permalink to this definition")
        :   A column is a sub-collection of the table that represents a group of
            same type data.

        FILESET *= 'fileset'*[¶](#gravitino.api.metadata_object.MetadataObject.Type.FILESET "Permalink to this definition")
        :   A fileset is mapped to a directory on a file system like HDFS, S3, ADLS,
            GCS, etc.

        METALAKE *= 'metalake'*[¶](#gravitino.api.metadata_object.MetadataObject.Type.METALAKE "Permalink to this definition")
        :   A metalake is a concept of tenant. It means an organization. A metalake
            contains many data sources.

        MODEL *= 'model'*[¶](#gravitino.api.metadata_object.MetadataObject.Type.MODEL "Permalink to this definition")
        :   A model is mapped to the model artifact in ML.

        ROLE *= 'role'*[¶](#gravitino.api.metadata_object.MetadataObject.Type.ROLE "Permalink to this definition")
        :   A role is an object contains specific securable objects with privileges.

        SCHEMA *= 'schema'*[¶](#gravitino.api.metadata_object.MetadataObject.Type.SCHEMA "Permalink to this definition")
        :   “A schema is a sub collection of the catalog. The schema can contain filesets,
            tables, topics, etc.

        TABLE *= 'table'*[¶](#gravitino.api.metadata_object.MetadataObject.Type.TABLE "Permalink to this definition")
        :   A table is mapped the table of relational data sources like Apache Hive,
            MySQL, etc.

        TOPIC *= 'topic'*[¶](#gravitino.api.metadata_object.MetadataObject.Type.TOPIC "Permalink to this definition")
        :   A topic is mapped the topic of messaging data sources like Apache Kafka,
            Apache Pulsar, etc.

    full\_name() → str[¶](#gravitino.api.metadata_object.MetadataObject.full_name "Permalink to this definition")
    :   The full name of the object.

        Full name will be separated by “.” to represent a string identifier of the object,
        like catalog, catalog.table, etc.

:   Bases: `ABC`

    Represents interface to get credentials.

    \_\_init\_\_()[¶](#gravitino.api.credential.supports_credentials.SupportsCredentials.__init__ "Permalink to this definition")

    Methods

    |  |  |
    | --- | --- |
    | [`__init__`](#gravitino.api.credential.supports_credentials.SupportsCredentials.__init__ "gravitino.api.credential.supports_credentials.SupportsCredentials.__init__")() |  |
    | [`get_credential`](#gravitino.api.credential.supports_credentials.SupportsCredentials.get_credential "gravitino.api.credential.supports_credentials.SupportsCredentials.get_credential")(credential\_type) | Retrieves Credential object based on the specified credential type. |
    | [`get_credentials`](#gravitino.api.credential.supports_credentials.SupportsCredentials.get_credentials "gravitino.api.credential.supports_credentials.SupportsCredentials.get_credentials")() | Retrieves a List of Credential objects. |

    get\_credential(*credential\_type: str*) → [Credential](gravitino.api.credential.credential.Credential.html#gravitino.api.credential.credential.Credential "gravitino.api.credential.credential.Credential")[¶](#gravitino.api.credential.supports_credentials.SupportsCredentials.get_credential "Permalink to this definition")
    :   Retrieves Credential object based on the specified credential type.

        Args:
        :   credential\_type: The type of the credential like s3-token,
            s3-secret-key which are defined in the specific credentials.

        Returns:
        :   An Credential object with the specified credential type.

        Raises:
        :   NoSuchCredentialException If the specific credential cannot be found.
            IllegalStateException if multiple credential can be found.

    *abstract* get\_credentials() → List[[Credential](gravitino.api.credential.credential.Credential.html#gravitino.api.credential.credential.Credential "gravitino.api.credential.credential.Credential")][¶](#gravitino.api.credential.supports_credentials.SupportsCredentials.get_credentials "Permalink to this definition")
    :   Retrieves a List of Credential objects.

        Returns:
        :   A List of Credential objects. In most cases the array only contains

        one credential. If the object like Fileset contains multiple locations
        for different storages like HDFS, S3, the array will contain multiple
        credentials. The array could be empty if you request a credential for
        a catalog but the credential provider couldn’t generate the credential
        for the catalog, like S3 token credential provider only generate
        credential for the specific object like Fileset,Table. There will be at
        most one credential for one credential type.

:   Bases: `ABC`

    Interface for supporting getting or associate tags to objects.

    This interface will be mixed with metadata objects to provide tag operations.

    \_\_init\_\_()[¶](#gravitino.api.tag.supports_tags.SupportsTags.__init__ "Permalink to this definition")

    Methods

    |  |  |
    | --- | --- |
    | [`__init__`](#gravitino.api.tag.supports_tags.SupportsTags.__init__ "gravitino.api.tag.supports_tags.SupportsTags.__init__")() |  |
    | [`associate_tags`](#gravitino.api.tag.supports_tags.SupportsTags.associate_tags "gravitino.api.tag.supports_tags.SupportsTags.associate_tags")(tags\_to\_add, tags\_to\_remove) | Associate tags to the specific object. |
    | [`get_tag`](#gravitino.api.tag.supports_tags.SupportsTags.get_tag "gravitino.api.tag.supports_tags.SupportsTags.get_tag")(name) | Get a tag by its name for the specific object. |
    | [`list_tags`](#gravitino.api.tag.supports_tags.SupportsTags.list_tags "gravitino.api.tag.supports_tags.SupportsTags.list_tags")() | List all the tag names for the specific object. |
    | [`list_tags_info`](#gravitino.api.tag.supports_tags.SupportsTags.list_tags_info "gravitino.api.tag.supports_tags.SupportsTags.list_tags_info")() | List all the tags with details for the specific object. |

    *abstract* associate\_tags(*tags\_to\_add: List[str]*, *tags\_to\_remove: List[str]*) → List[str][¶](#gravitino.api.tag.supports_tags.SupportsTags.associate_tags "Permalink to this definition")
    :   Associate tags to the specific object.

        The tags\_to\_add will be added to the object, and the tags\_to\_remove will be removed from the object.

        Note that:
        1. Adding or removing tags that are not existed will be ignored.
        2. If the same name tag is in both tags\_to\_add and tags\_to\_remove, it will be ignored.
        3. If the tag is already associated with the object, it will raise TagAlreadyAssociatedException.

        Args:
        :   tags\_to\_add (List[str]): The arrays of tag name to be added to the object.
            tags\_to\_remove (List[str]): The array of tag name to be removed from the object.

        Raises:
        :   TagAlreadyAssociatedException: If the tag is already associated with the object.

        Returns:
        :   List[str]: The array of tag names that are associated with the object.

    *abstract* get\_tag(*name: str*) → [Tag](gravitino.api.tag.tag.Tag.html#gravitino.api.tag.tag.Tag "gravitino.api.tag.tag.Tag")[¶](#gravitino.api.tag.supports_tags.SupportsTags.get_tag "Permalink to this definition")
    :   Get a tag by its name for the specific object.

        Args:
        :   name (str): The name of the tag.

        Raises:
        :   NoSuchTagException: If the tag does not associate with the object.

        Returns:
        :   Tag: The tag.

    *abstract* list\_tags() → List[str][¶](#gravitino.api.tag.supports_tags.SupportsTags.list_tags "Permalink to this definition")
    :   List all the tag names for the specific object.

    | [`URI_NAME_UNKNOWN`](#gravitino.api.model.model_version.ModelVersion.URI_NAME_UNKNOWN "gravitino.api.model.model_version.ModelVersion.URI_NAME_UNKNOWN") | The reserved URI name to indicate the URI name is unknown. |

    *abstract* aliases() → List[str][¶](#gravitino.api.model.model_version.ModelVersion.aliases "Permalink to this definition")
    :   The aliases of this model version. The aliases are the alternative names of the model version.
        The aliases are optional. The aliases are unique for a model version. If the alias is already
        set to one model version, it cannot be set to another model version.

        Returns:
        :   The aliases of the model version.

    *abstract* comment() → str | None[¶](#gravitino.api.model.model_version.ModelVersion.comment "Permalink to this definition")
    :   The comment of this model version. This comment can be different from the comment of the model
        to provide more detailed information about this version.

        Returns:
        :   The comment of the model version. None is returned if no comment is set.

    properties() → Dict[str, str][¶](#gravitino.api.model.model_version.ModelVersion.properties "Permalink to this definition")
    :   The properties of the model version. The properties are key-value pairs that can be used to
        store additional information of the model version. The properties are optional.

        Returns:
        :   The properties of the model version. An empty dictionary is returned if no properties are set.

    uri() → str[¶](#gravitino.api.model.model_version.ModelVersion.uri "Permalink to this definition")
    :   The unnamed URI of the model artifact. The URI is the location of the model artifact. The URI can be a
        file path or a remote URI.

        Returns:
        :   The URI of the model artifact.

    *abstract* uris() → Dict[str, str][¶](#gravitino.api.model.model_version.ModelVersion.uris "Permalink to this definition")
    :   The name and corresponding URI of the model artifact. The key is the name of the URI, and the
        value is the location of the model artifact, which can be a file path or a remote URI.

        The “unknown” URI name is reserved for the compatibility with single URI.

        Returns:
        :   The URIs of the model version, the key is the name of the URI and the value is the URI of
            the model artifact.

    *abstract* version() → int[¶](#gravitino.api.model.model_version.ModelVersion.version "Permalink to this definition")
    :   The version of this model object. The version number is an integer number starts from 0. Each
        time the model checkpoint / snapshot is linked to the registered, the version number will be
        increased by 1.

        Returns:
        :   The version of the model object.

    An interface representing a schema in the Catalog. A Schema is a
    basic container of relational objects, like tables, views, etc. A Schema can be self-nested,
    which means it can be schema1.schema2.table.

        been constructed without all the required fields present.

        Raises:
        :   IllegalArgumentException: If the message is not valid.

    Fileset catalog is a catalog implementation that supports fileset like metadata operations, for
    example, schemas and filesets list, creation, update and deletion. A Fileset catalog is under the metalake.

    | `rest_client` |  |

    PROPERTY\_PACKAGE *= 'package'*[¶](#gravitino.client.fileset_catalog.FilesetCatalog.PROPERTY_PACKAGE "Permalink to this definition")
    :   A reserved property to specify the package location of the catalog. The “package” is a string
        of path to the folder where all the catalog related dependencies is located. The dependencies
        under the “package” will be loaded by Gravitino to create the catalog.

        The property “package” is not needed if the catalog is a built-in one, Gravitino will search
        the proper location using “provider” to load the dependencies. Only when the folder is in
        different location, the “package” property is needed.

    *class* Type(*value*)[¶](#gravitino.client.fileset_catalog.FilesetCatalog.Type "Permalink to this definition")
    :   Bases: `Enum`

        The type of the catalog.

        FILESET *= ('fileset', True)*[¶](#gravitino.client.fileset_catalog.FilesetCatalog.Type.FILESET "Permalink to this definition")
        :   Catalog Type for Fileset System (including HDFS, S3, etc.), like path/to/file

        MESSAGING *= ('messaging', False)*[¶](#gravitino.client.fileset_catalog.FilesetCatalog.Type.MESSAGING "Permalink to this definition")
        :   Catalog Type for Message Queue, like kafka://topic

        MODEL *= ('model', True)*[¶](#gravitino.client.fileset_catalog.FilesetCatalog.Type.MODEL "Permalink to this definition")
        :   Catalog Type for ML model

        RELATIONAL *= ('relational', False)*[¶](#gravitino.client.fileset_catalog.FilesetCatalog.Type.RELATIONAL "Permalink to this definition")
        :   “Catalog Type for Relational Data Structure, like db.table, catalog.db.table.

        UNSUPPORTED *= ('unsupported', False)*[¶](#gravitino.client.fileset_catalog.FilesetCatalog.Type.UNSUPPORTED "Permalink to this definition")
        :   Catalog Type for test only.

        *property* supports\_managed\_catalog[¶](#gravitino.client.fileset_catalog.FilesetCatalog.Type.supports_managed_catalog "Permalink to this definition")
        :   A flag to indicate if the catalog type supports managed catalog. Managed catalog is a
            concept in Gravitino, which means Gravitino will manage the lifecycle of the catalog
            and its subsidiaries. If the catalog type supports managed catalog, users can create
            managed catalog of this type without specifying the catalog provider, Gravitino will
            use the type as the provider to create the managed catalog. If the catalog type does
            not support managed catalog, users need to specify the provider to create the catalog.

        *property* type\_name[¶](#gravitino.client.fileset_catalog.FilesetCatalog.Type.type_name "Permalink to this definition")
        :   The name of the catalog type.

    :   Create a fileset metadata in the catalog.

        If the type of the fileset object is “MANAGED”, the underlying storageLocation can be null,
        and Gravitino will manage the storage location based on the location of the schema.

        If the type of the fileset object is “EXTERNAL”, the underlying storageLocation must be set.

        Args:
        :   ident: A fileset identifier, which should be “schema.fileset” format.
            comment: The comment of the fileset.
            fileset\_type: The type of the fileset.
            storage\_location: The storage location of the fileset.
            properties: The properties of the fileset.

        Raises:
        :   NoSuchSchemaException If the schema does not exist.
            FilesetAlreadyExistsException If the fileset already exists.

        Returns:

# gravitino.api.file.fileset.Fileset[¶](#gravitino-api-file-fileset-fileset "Permalink to this heading")

*class* gravitino.api.file.fileset.Fileset[¶](#gravitino.api.file.fileset.Fileset "Permalink to this definition")
:   Bases: [`Auditable`](gravitino.api.auditable.Auditable.html#gravitino.api.auditable.Auditable "gravitino.api.auditable.Auditable")

    An interface representing a fileset under a schema Namespace. A fileset is a virtual
    concept of the file or directory that is managed by Gravitino. Users can create a fileset object
    to manage the non-tabular data on the FS-like storage. The typical use case is to manage the
    training data for AI workloads. The major difference compare to the relational table is that the
    fileset is schema-free, the main property of the fileset is the storage location of the
    underlying data.

    Fileset defines the basic properties of a fileset object. A catalog implementation
    with FilesetCatalog should implement this interface.

    \_\_init\_\_()[¶](#gravitino.api.file.fileset.Fileset.__init__ "Permalink to this definition")

    Methods

    |  |  |
    | --- | --- |

    | [`properties`](#gravitino.api.file.fileset.Fileset.properties "gravitino.api.file.fileset.Fileset.properties")() | Returns: |
    | [`storage_location`](#gravitino.api.file.fileset.Fileset.storage_location "gravitino.api.file.fileset.Fileset.storage_location")() | Get the unnamed storage location of the file or directory path managed by this fileset object. |
    | [`storage_locations`](#gravitino.api.file.fileset.Fileset.storage_locations "gravitino.api.file.fileset.Fileset.storage_locations")() | Get the storage location name and corresponding path of the file or directory path that is managed by this fileset object. |

    *abstract* properties() → Dict[str, str][¶](#gravitino.api.file.fileset.Fileset.properties "Permalink to this definition")
    :   Returns:
        :   The properties of the fileset object. Empty map is returned if no properties are set.

    storage\_location() → str[¶](#gravitino.api.file.fileset.Fileset.storage_location "Permalink to this definition")
    :   Get the unnamed storage location of the file or directory path managed by this fileset object.

        The returned storageLocation can be either the one specified when creating the fileset object
        (using storageLocation field or storageLocations field), or the one specified at the catalog/schema
        level (using property “location” or properties with prefix “location-”) if the fileset object is
        created under this catalog/schema.

        The storageLocation at each level can contain placeholders, formatted as {{name}}, which will
        be replaced by the corresponding fileset property value when the fileset object is created.
        The placeholder property in the fileset object is formed as “placeholder-{{name}}”. For example,
        if the storageLocation is “<file:///path>/{{schema}}-{{fileset}}-{{version}}”, and the fileset
        object “catalog1.schema1.fileset1” has the property “placeholder-version” set to “v1”,
        then the storageLocation will be “<file:///path/schema1-fileset1-v1>”.

        For managed fileset, the storageLocation can be:

        1. The one specified when creating the fileset object, and the placeholders in the
           storageLocation will be replaced by the placeholder value specified in the fileset properties.
        2. When catalog property “location” is specified but schema property “location” is not specified,
           then the storageLocation will be:

           > 1. “{catalog location}/schemaName/filesetName” - if {catalog location} has no placeholders
           > 2. “{catalog location}” - placeholders in {catalog location} will be replaced by values
           >    specified in fileset properties
        3. When catalog property “location” is not specified but schema property “location” is specified,
           then the storageLocation will be:

           > 1. “{schema location}/filesetName” - if {schema location} has no placeholders
           > 2. “{schema location}” - placeholders in {schema location} will be replaced by values
           >    specified in fileset properties
        4. When both catalog property “location” and schema property “location” are specified,
           then the storageLocation will be:

           > 1. “{schema location}/filesetName” - if {schema location} has no placeholders
           > 2. “{schema location}” - placeholders in {schema location} will be replaced by values
           >    specified in fileset properties

        5) null value - when catalog property “location”, schema property “location”, storageLocation
        field of fileset, and “unknown” location in storageLocations are not specified.

        For external fileset, the storageLocation can be:
        1) The one specified when creating the fileset object, and the placeholders in the

        > storageLocation will be replaced by the placeholder value specified in the fileset properties.

        Returns:
        :   str: The storage location of the fileset object.

    *abstract* storage\_locations() → Dict[str, str][¶](#gravitino.api.file.fileset.Fileset.storage_locations "Permalink to this definition")
    :   Get the storage location name and corresponding path of the file or directory path that is
        managed by this fileset object. The key is the name of the storage location and the value is
        the storage location path.

        Each storageLocation in the values can either be the one specified when creating the fileset
        object, or the one specified in the catalog / schema level if the fileset object is created
        under this catalog / schema.

        The “unknown” location name is reserved to indicate the default storage location of the fileset.
        It can be specified in catalog / schema level by the property “location” or in the fileset level
        by the field “storageLocation”. Other location names can be specified in the fileset level by the
        key-value pairs in the field “storageLocations”, and by “location-{name}” properties in the
        catalog / schema level.

        The storageLocation at each level can contain placeholders, formatted as {{name}}, which will
        be replaced by the corresponding fileset property value when the fileset object is created.
        The placeholder property in the fileset object is formed as “placeholder-{{name}}”. For example,
        if the storageLocation is “<file:///path>/{{schema}}-{{fileset}}-{{version}}”, and the fileset
        object “catalog1.schema1.fileset1” has the property “placeholder-version” set to “v1”,
        then the storageLocation will be “<file:///path/schema1-fileset1-v1>”.

        For managed fileset, the storageLocation can be:

        1. The one specified when creating the fileset object, and the placeholders in the
           storageLocation will be replaced by the placeholder value specified in the fileset properties.
        2. When catalog property “location” is specified but schema property “location” is not specified,
           then the storageLocation will be:

           > 1. “{catalog location}/schemaName/filesetName” - if {catalog location} has no placeholders
           > 2. “{catalog location}” - placeholders in {catalog location} will be replaced by values
           >    specified in fileset properties
        3. When catalog property “location” is not specified but schema property “location” is specified,
           then the storageLocation will be:

           > 1. “{schema location}/filesetName” - if {schema location} has no placeholders
           > 2. “{schema location}” - placeholders in {schema location} will be replaced by values
           >    specified in fileset properties
        4. When both catalog property “location” and schema property “location” are specified,
           then the storageLocation will be:

           > 1. “{schema location}/filesetName” - if {schema location} has no placeholders
           > 2. “{schema location}” - placeholders in {schema location} will be replaced by values
           >    specified in fileset properties
        5. When there is no location specified in catalog level, schema level, storageLocation of fileset,
           and storageLocations of fileset at the same time, this situation is illegal.

        For external fileset, the storageLocation can be:
        1) The one specified when creating the fileset object, and the placeholders in the

        > storageLocation will be replaced by the placeholder value specified in the fileset properties.

        Returns:
        :   The storage locations of the fileset object, the key is the name of the storage

        location and the value is the storage location path.

    *abstract* type() → [Type](#gravitino.api.file.fileset.Fileset.Type "gravitino.api.file.fileset.Fileset.Type")[¶](#gravitino.api.file.fileset.Fileset.type "Permalink to this definition")
    :   @Returns:
        :   The type of the fileset object.

        object, the return value will be present. Otherwise, it will be empty.

    BaseSchemaCatalog is the base abstract class for all the catalog with schema. It provides the
    common methods for managing schemas in a catalog. With BaseSchemaCatalog, users can list,
    create, load, alter and drop a schema with specified identifier.

    | `rest_client` |  |

    PROPERTY\_PACKAGE *= 'package'*[¶](#gravitino.client.base_schema_catalog.BaseSchemaCatalog.PROPERTY_PACKAGE "Permalink to this definition")
    :   A reserved property to specify the package location of the catalog. The “package” is a string
        of path to the folder where all the catalog related dependencies is located. The dependencies
        under the “package” will be loaded by Gravitino to create the catalog.

        The property “package” is not needed if the catalog is a built-in one, Gravitino will search
        the proper location using “provider” to load the dependencies. Only when the folder is in
        different location, the “package” property is needed.

    *class* Type(*value*)[¶](#gravitino.client.base_schema_catalog.BaseSchemaCatalog.Type "Permalink to this definition")
    :   Bases: `Enum`

        The type of the catalog.

        FILESET *= ('fileset', True)*[¶](#gravitino.client.base_schema_catalog.BaseSchemaCatalog.Type.FILESET "Permalink to this definition")
        :   Catalog Type for Fileset System (including HDFS, S3, etc.), like path/to/file

        MESSAGING *= ('messaging', False)*[¶](#gravitino.client.base_schema_catalog.BaseSchemaCatalog.Type.MESSAGING "Permalink to this definition")
        :   Catalog Type for Message Queue, like kafka://topic

        MODEL *= ('model', True)*[¶](#gravitino.client.base_schema_catalog.BaseSchemaCatalog.Type.MODEL "Permalink to this definition")
        :   Catalog Type for ML model

        RELATIONAL *= ('relational', False)*[¶](#gravitino.client.base_schema_catalog.BaseSchemaCatalog.Type.RELATIONAL "Permalink to this definition")
        :   “Catalog Type for Relational Data Structure, like db.table, catalog.db.table.

        UNSUPPORTED *= ('unsupported', False)*[¶](#gravitino.client.base_schema_catalog.BaseSchemaCatalog.Type.UNSUPPORTED "Permalink to this definition")
        :   Catalog Type for test only.

        *property* supports\_managed\_catalog[¶](#gravitino.client.base_schema_catalog.BaseSchemaCatalog.Type.supports_managed_catalog "Permalink to this definition")
        :   A flag to indicate if the catalog type supports managed catalog. Managed catalog is a
            concept in Gravitino, which means Gravitino will manage the lifecycle of the catalog
            and its subsidiaries. If the catalog type supports managed catalog, users can create
            managed catalog of this type without specifying the catalog provider, Gravitino will
            use the type as the provider to create the managed catalog. If the catalog type does
            not support managed catalog, users need to specify the provider to create the catalog.

        *property* type\_name[¶](#gravitino.client.base_schema_catalog.BaseSchemaCatalog.Type.type_name "Permalink to this definition")
        :   The name of the catalog type.

    *class* Type(*value*)[¶](#gravitino.client.metadata_object_impl.MetadataObjectImpl.Type "Permalink to this definition")
    :   Bases: `Enum`

        The type of object in the Gravitino system. Every type will map one
        kind of the entity of the underlying system.

        CATALOG *= 'catalog'*[¶](#gravitino.client.metadata_object_impl.MetadataObjectImpl.Type.CATALOG "Permalink to this definition")
        :   A catalog is a collection of metadata from a specific metadata source,
            like Apache Hive catalog, Apache Iceberg catalog, JDBC catalog, etc.

        COLUMN *= 'column'*[¶](#gravitino.client.metadata_object_impl.MetadataObjectImpl.Type.COLUMN "Permalink to this definition")
        :   A column is a sub-collection of the table that represents a group of
            same type data.

        FILESET *= 'fileset'*[¶](#gravitino.client.metadata_object_impl.MetadataObjectImpl.Type.FILESET "Permalink to this definition")
        :   A fileset is mapped to a directory on a file system like HDFS, S3, ADLS,
            GCS, etc.

        METALAKE *= 'metalake'*[¶](#gravitino.client.metadata_object_impl.MetadataObjectImpl.Type.METALAKE "Permalink to this definition")
        :   A metalake is a concept of tenant. It means an organization. A metalake
            contains many data sources.

        MODEL *= 'model'*[¶](#gravitino.client.metadata_object_impl.MetadataObjectImpl.Type.MODEL "Permalink to this definition")
        :   A model is mapped to the model artifact in ML.

        ROLE *= 'role'*[¶](#gravitino.client.metadata_object_impl.MetadataObjectImpl.Type.ROLE "Permalink to this definition")
        :   A role is an object contains specific securable objects with privileges.

        SCHEMA *= 'schema'*[¶](#gravitino.client.metadata_object_impl.MetadataObjectImpl.Type.SCHEMA "Permalink to this definition")
        :   “A schema is a sub collection of the catalog. The schema can contain filesets,
            tables, topics, etc.

        TABLE *= 'table'*[¶](#gravitino.client.metadata_object_impl.MetadataObjectImpl.Type.TABLE "Permalink to this definition")
        :   A table is mapped the table of relational data sources like Apache Hive,
            MySQL, etc.

        TOPIC *= 'topic'*[¶](#gravitino.client.metadata_object_impl.MetadataObjectImpl.Type.TOPIC "Permalink to this definition")
        :   A topic is mapped the topic of messaging data sources like Apache Kafka,
            Apache Pulsar, etc.

    full\_name() → str[¶](#gravitino.client.metadata_object_impl.MetadataObjectImpl.full_name "Permalink to this definition")
    :   The full name of the object.

        Full name will be separated by “.” to represent a string identifier of the object,
        like catalog, catalog.table, etc.

    name() → str[¶](#gravitino.client.metadata_object_impl.MetadataObjectImpl.name "Permalink to this definition")

    provide the ability to manage job templates and jobs within the Gravitino system.

    alter\_job\_template(*job\_template\_name: str*, *\*changes: [JobTemplateChange](gravitino.api.job.job_template_change.JobTemplateChange.html#gravitino.api.job.job_template_change.JobTemplateChange "gravitino.api.job.job_template_change.JobTemplateChange")*) → [JobTemplate](gravitino.api.job.job_template.JobTemplate.html#gravitino.api.job.job_template.JobTemplate "gravitino.api.job.job_template.JobTemplate")[¶](#gravitino.api.job.supports_jobs.SupportsJobs.alter_job_template "Permalink to this definition")
    :   Alters a job template by applying the specified changes. This allows for modifying the
        properties of an existing job template, such as its name, description, or parameters.

        Args:
        :   job\_template\_name: The name of the job template.
            changes: The changes to apply to the job template.

        Raises:
        :   NoSuchJobTemplateException: If the job template does not exist.
            IllegalArgumentException: If any of the changes cannot be applied to the job template.

        Returns:
        :   The altered job template.

    *abstract* cancel\_job(*job\_id: str*) → [JobHandle](gravitino.api.job.job_handle.JobHandle.html#gravitino.api.job.job_handle.JobHandle "gravitino.api.job.job_handle.JobHandle")[¶](#gravitino.api.job.supports_jobs.SupportsJobs.cancel_job "Permalink to this definition")
    :   Cancels a running job by its ID. This operation will attempt to cancel the job if it is
        still running. This method will return immediately, user could use the job handle to
        check the status of the job after invoking this method.

        Args:
        :   job\_id: The ID of the job to cancel.

        Raises:
        :   NoSuchJobException: If no job with the specified ID exists.

    *abstract* delete\_job\_template(*job\_template\_name: str*) → bool[¶](#gravitino.api.job.supports_jobs.SupportsJobs.delete_job_template "Permalink to this definition")
    :   Deletes a job template by its name. This will remove the job template from Gravitino, and it
        will no longer be available for execution. Only when all the jobs associated with this job
        template are completed, failed or cancelled, the job template can be deleted successfully,
        otherwise it will return false.

        The deletion of a job template will also delete all the jobs associated with this template.

        Args:
        :   job\_template\_name: The name of the job template to delete.

        Returns:
        :   bool: True if the job template was deleted successfully, False if the job template
            does not exist.

        Raises:
        :   InUseException: If there are still queued or started jobs associated with this job template.

    *abstract* get\_job(*job\_id: str*) → [JobHandle](gravitino.api.job.job_handle.JobHandle.html#gravitino.api.job.job_handle.JobHandle "gravitino.api.job.job_handle.JobHandle")[¶](#gravitino.api.job.supports_jobs.SupportsJobs.get_job "Permalink to this definition")
    :   Retrieves a job by its ID.

        Args:
        :   job\_id: The ID of the job to retrieve.

        Returns:
        :   JobHandle: The handle representing the job with the specified ID.

        Raises:
        :   NoSuchJobException: If no job with the specified ID exists.

    *abstract* get\_job\_template(*job\_template\_name: str*) → [JobTemplate](gravitino.api.job.job_template.JobTemplate.html#gravitino.api.job.job_template.JobTemplate "gravitino.api.job.job_template.JobTemplate")[¶](#gravitino.api.job.supports_jobs.SupportsJobs.get_job_template "Permalink to this definition")
    :   Retrieves a job template by its name.

        Args:
        :   job\_template\_name: The name of the job template to retrieve.

        Returns:
        :   The job template if found, otherwise raises an exception.

        Raises:
        :   NoSuchJobTemplateException: If no job template with the specified name exists.

    *abstract* list\_job\_templates() → List[[JobTemplate](gravitino.api.job.job_template.JobTemplate.html#gravitino.api.job.job_template.JobTemplate "gravitino.api.job.job_template.JobTemplate")][¶](#gravitino.api.job.supports_jobs.SupportsJobs.list_job_templates "Permalink to this definition")
    :   Lists all the registered job templates in Gravitino.

        Returns:
        :   List of job templates.

    *abstract* list\_jobs(*job\_template\_name: str | None = None*) → List[[JobHandle](gravitino.api.job.job_handle.JobHandle.html#gravitino.api.job.job_handle.JobHandle "gravitino.api.job.job_handle.JobHandle")][¶](#gravitino.api.job.supports_jobs.SupportsJobs.list_jobs "Permalink to this definition")
    :   Lists all the jobs in Gravitino. If a job template name is provided, it will filter the jobs
        by that template.

        Args:
        :   job\_template\_name: Optional; if provided, only jobs associated with this template will be listed.

        Returns:
        :   List of JobHandle objects representing the jobs.

    *abstract* register\_job\_template(*job\_template*) → None[¶](#gravitino.api.job.supports_jobs.SupportsJobs.register_job_template "Permalink to this definition")
    :   Register a job template with the specified job template to Gravitino. The registered
        job will be maintained in Gravitino, allowing it to be executed later.

        Args:
        :   job\_template: The job template to register.

        Raises:
        :   JobTemplateAlreadyExists: If a job template with the same name already exists.

    *abstract* run\_job(*job\_template\_name: str*, *job\_conf: Dict[str, str]*) → [JobHandle](gravitino.api.job.job_handle.JobHandle.html#gravitino.api.job.job_handle.JobHandle "gravitino.api.job.job_handle.JobHandle")[¶](#gravitino.api.job.supports_jobs.SupportsJobs.run_job "Permalink to this definition")
    :   Run a job with the template name and configuration. The jobConf is a map of key-value
        contains the variables that will be used to replace the templated parameters in the job
        template.

        Args:
        :   job\_template\_name: The name of the job template to run.
            job\_conf: A dictionary containing the job configuration parameters.

        Returns:
        :   JobHandle: A handle to the running job, which can be used to monitor or manage the job.

        Raises:
        :   NoSuchJobTemplateException: If no job template with the specified name exists.

:   Bases: `Enum`

    JobType is an enum to define the type of the job.

    Gravitino supports different types of jobs, such as Spark and Shell. The job type is
    required to determine the runtime environment for executing the job.

# gravitino.api.rel.indexes.index.Index[¶](#gravitino-api-rel-indexes-index-index "Permalink to this heading")

*class* gravitino.api.rel.indexes.index.Index[¶](#gravitino.api.rel.indexes.index.Index "Permalink to this definition")
:   Bases: `ABC`

    The Index interface defines methods for implementing table index columns.

    Currently, settings for PRIMARY\_KEY and UNIQUE\_KEY are provided.

    \_\_init\_\_()[¶](#gravitino.api.rel.indexes.index.Index.__init__ "Permalink to this definition")

    Methods

    |  |  |
    | --- | --- |
    | [`__init__`](#gravitino.api.rel.indexes.index.Index.__init__ "gravitino.api.rel.indexes.index.Index.__init__")() |  |
    | [`field_names`](#gravitino.api.rel.indexes.index.Index.field_names "gravitino.api.rel.indexes.index.Index.field_names")() | Returns the field name under the table contained in the index. |
    | [`name`](#gravitino.api.rel.indexes.index.Index.name "gravitino.api.rel.indexes.index.Index.name")() | Returns the name of the index. |
    | [`type`](#gravitino.api.rel.indexes.index.Index.type "gravitino.api.rel.indexes.index.Index.type")() | Returns the type of the index. |

    *class* IndexType(*value*)[¶](#gravitino.api.rel.indexes.index.Index.IndexType "Permalink to this definition")
    :   Bases: `str`, `Enum`

        The enum IndexType defines the type of the index.

        Currently, PRIMARY\_KEY and UNIQUE\_KEY are supported.

        PRIMARY\_KEY *= 'PRIMARY\_KEY'*[¶](#gravitino.api.rel.indexes.index.Index.IndexType.PRIMARY_KEY "Permalink to this definition")
        :   PRIMARY KEY index in a relational database is a field or a combination of fields that
            uniquely identifies each record in a table. It serves as a unique identifier for each row,
            ensuring that no two rows have the same key. The PRIMARY KEY is used to establish
            relationships between tables and enforce the entity integrity of a database. Additionally, it
            helps in indexing and organizing the data for efficient retrieval and maintenance.

        UNIQUE\_KEY *= 'UNIQUE\_KEY'*[¶](#gravitino.api.rel.indexes.index.Index.IndexType.UNIQUE_KEY "Permalink to this definition")
        :   UNIQUE KEY in a relational database is a field or a combination of fields that ensures each
            record in a table has a distinct value or combination of values. Unlike a primary key, a
            UNIQUE KEY allows for the presence of null values, but it still enforces the constraint that
            no two records can have the same unique key value(s). UNIQUE KEYs are used to maintain data
            integrity by preventing duplicate entries in specific columns, and they can be applied to
            columns that are not designated as the primary key. The uniqueness constraint imposed by
            UNIQUE KEY helps in avoiding redundancy and ensuring data accuracy in the database.

    *abstract* field\_names() → List[List[str]][¶](#gravitino.api.rel.indexes.index.Index.field_names "Permalink to this definition")
    :   Returns the field name under the table contained in the index.

        It is the column names, could be “a.b.c” for nested column, but normally it
        could only be “a”.

        Returns:
        :   List[List[str]]: The field name under the table contained in the index.

    *abstract* name() → str | None[¶](#gravitino.api.rel.indexes.index.Index.name "Permalink to this definition")
    :   Returns the name of the index.

        Returns:
        :   Optional[str]: The name of the index.

    *abstract* type() → [IndexType](#gravitino.api.rel.indexes.index.Index.IndexType "gravitino.api.rel.indexes.index.Index.IndexType")[¶](#gravitino.api.rel.indexes.index.Index.type "Permalink to this definition")
    :   Returns the type of the index. eg: PRIMARY\_KEY and UNIQUE\_KEY.

        Returns:
        :   IndexType: The type of the index. eg: PRIMARY\_KEY and UNIQUE\_KEY.

# gravitino.filesystem.gvfs\_base\_operations.FileSystemCacheKey[¶](#gravitino-filesystem-gvfs-base-operations-filesystemcachekey "Permalink to this heading")

*class* gravitino.filesystem.gvfs\_base\_operations.FileSystemCacheKey(*scheme: str*, *authority: str | None*, *credentials*, *catalog\_props: Dict[str, str]*, *options: Dict[str, str]*, *extra\_kwargs: Dict*)[¶](#gravitino.filesystem.gvfs_base_operations.FileSystemCacheKey "Permalink to this definition")
:   Bases: `object`

    A cache key for filesystem instances following fsspec’s native caching behavior.

    This key is based on:
    - Process ID (ensures cache is process-specific, like fsspec)
    - Thread ID (ensures thread-specific caching, like fsspec)
    - Filesystem scheme (e.g., ‘s3’, ‘gs’, ‘hdfs’, ‘file’)
    - Authority (e.g., bucket name, host:port)
    - Configuration token (hashable representation of credentials and config)

    This matches fsspec’s \_Cached metaclass caching strategy which includes both
    process ID and thread ID in the cache key. While this differs from Java GVFS
    (which shares filesystems across threads), it provides better thread isolation
    and matches Python’s ecosystem conventions.

    \_\_init\_\_(*scheme: str*, *authority: str | None*, *credentials*, *catalog\_props: Dict[str, str]*, *options: Dict[str, str]*, *extra\_kwargs: Dict*)[¶](#gravitino.filesystem.gvfs_base_operations.FileSystemCacheKey.__init__ "Permalink to this definition")
    :   Initialize a FileSystemCacheKey.

        Args:
        :   scheme: The filesystem scheme (e.g., ‘s3’, ‘gs’, ‘hdfs’, ‘file’)
            authority: The authority part of the URI (e.g., bucket name, host:port)
            credentials: The credentials for the filesystem
            catalog\_props: The catalog properties
            options: The GVFS options
            extra\_kwargs: Extra keyword arguments

    Methods

# gravitino.api.rel.table\_change.RenameColumn[¶](#gravitino-api-rel-table-change-renamecolumn "Permalink to this heading")

*final class* gravitino.api.rel.table\_change.RenameColumn(*\_field\_name: list[str]*, *\_new\_name: str*)[¶](#gravitino.api.rel.table_change.RenameColumn "Permalink to this definition")
:   Bases: [`ColumnChange`](gravitino.api.rel.table_change.TableChange.html#gravitino.api.rel.table_change.TableChange.ColumnChange "gravitino.api.rel.table_change.TableChange.ColumnChange")

    A TableChange to rename a field.

    The name is used to find the field to rename. The new name will replace the **leaf field name**.
    For example, rename\_column(“a.b.c”, “x”) should produce column **a.b.x**.

    If the field does not exist, the change must result in an IllegalArgumentException.

*class* gravitino.client.gravitino\_client.GravitinoClient(*uri: str*, *metalake\_name: str*, *check\_version: bool = True*, *auth\_data\_provider: [AuthDataProvider](gravitino.auth.auth_data_provider.AuthDataProvider.html#gravitino.auth.auth_data_provider.AuthDataProvider "gravitino.auth.auth_data_provider.AuthDataProvider") | None = None*, *request\_headers: dict | None = None*, *client\_config: dict | None = None*)[¶](#gravitino.client.gravitino_client.GravitinoClient "Permalink to this definition")
:   Bases: [`GravitinoClientBase`](gravitino.client.gravitino_client_base.GravitinoClientBase.html#gravitino.client.gravitino_client_base.GravitinoClientBase "gravitino.client.gravitino_client_base.GravitinoClientBase"), [`SupportsJobs`](gravitino.api.job.supports_jobs.SupportsJobs.html#gravitino.api.job.supports_jobs.SupportsJobs "gravitino.api.job.supports_jobs.SupportsJobs")

    Gravitino Client for a user to interact with the Gravitino API, allowing the client to list,
    load, create, and alter Catalog.

    It uses an underlying [{@link](mailto:{%40link) RESTClient} to send HTTP requests and receive responses from the API.

    \_\_init\_\_(*uri: str*, *metalake\_name: str*, *check\_version: bool = True*, *auth\_data\_provider: [AuthDataProvider](gravitino.auth.auth_data_provider.AuthDataProvider.html#gravitino.auth.auth_data_provider.AuthDataProvider "gravitino.auth.auth_data_provider.AuthDataProvider") | None = None*, *request\_headers: dict | None = None*, *client\_config: dict | None = None*)[¶](#gravitino.client.gravitino_client.GravitinoClient.__init__ "Permalink to this definition")
    :   Constructs a new GravitinoClient with the given URI, authenticator and AuthDataProvider.

        Args:
        :   uri: The base URI for the Gravitino API.
            metalake\_name: The specified metalake name.
            auth\_data\_provider: The provider of the data which is used for authentication.
            request\_headers: The headers to be included in the HTTP requests.
            client\_config: The config properties for the HTTP Client

        Raises:
        :   NoSuchMetalakeException if the metalake with specified name does not exist.

    delete\_job\_template(*job\_template\_name: str*) → bool[¶](#gravitino.client.gravitino_client.GravitinoClient.delete_job_template "Permalink to this definition")
    :   Deletes a job template by its name. This will remove the job template from Gravitino, and it
        will no longer be available for execution. Only when all the jobs associated with this job
        template are completed, failed or cancelled, the job template can be deleted successfully,
        otherwise it will throw InUseException. Returns false if the job template to be deleted does
        not exist.

        The deletion of a job template will also delete all the jobs associated with this template.

        Args:
        :   job\_template\_name: The name of the job template to delete.

        Returns:
        :   bool: True if the job template was deleted successfully, False if the job template
            does not exist.

        Raises:
        :   InUseException: If there are still queued or started jobs associated with this job template.

    | [`PROPERTY_PACKAGE`](#gravitino.dto.catalog_dto.CatalogDTO.PROPERTY_PACKAGE "gravitino.dto.catalog_dto.CatalogDTO.PROPERTY_PACKAGE") | A reserved property to specify the package location of the catalog. |

    PROPERTY\_PACKAGE *= 'package'*[¶](#gravitino.dto.catalog_dto.CatalogDTO.PROPERTY_PACKAGE "Permalink to this definition")
    :   A reserved property to specify the package location of the catalog. The “package” is a string
        of path to the folder where all the catalog related dependencies is located. The dependencies
        under the “package” will be loaded by Gravitino to create the catalog.

        The property “package” is not needed if the catalog is a built-in one, Gravitino will search
        the proper location using “provider” to load the dependencies. Only when the folder is in
        different location, the “package” property is needed.

    *class* Type(*value*)[¶](#gravitino.dto.catalog_dto.CatalogDTO.Type "Permalink to this definition")
    :   Bases: `Enum`

        The type of the catalog.

        FILESET *= ('fileset', True)*[¶](#gravitino.dto.catalog_dto.CatalogDTO.Type.FILESET "Permalink to this definition")
        :   Catalog Type for Fileset System (including HDFS, S3, etc.), like path/to/file

        MESSAGING *= ('messaging', False)*[¶](#gravitino.dto.catalog_dto.CatalogDTO.Type.MESSAGING "Permalink to this definition")
        :   Catalog Type for Message Queue, like kafka://topic

        MODEL *= ('model', True)*[¶](#gravitino.dto.catalog_dto.CatalogDTO.Type.MODEL "Permalink to this definition")
        :   Catalog Type for ML model

        RELATIONAL *= ('relational', False)*[¶](#gravitino.dto.catalog_dto.CatalogDTO.Type.RELATIONAL "Permalink to this definition")
        :   “Catalog Type for Relational Data Structure, like db.table, catalog.db.table.

        UNSUPPORTED *= ('unsupported', False)*[¶](#gravitino.dto.catalog_dto.CatalogDTO.Type.UNSUPPORTED "Permalink to this definition")
        :   Catalog Type for test only.

        *property* supports\_managed\_catalog[¶](#gravitino.dto.catalog_dto.CatalogDTO.Type.supports_managed_catalog "Permalink to this definition")
        :   A flag to indicate if the catalog type supports managed catalog. Managed catalog is a
            concept in Gravitino, which means Gravitino will manage the lifecycle of the catalog
            and its subsidiaries. If the catalog type supports managed catalog, users can create
            managed catalog of this type without specifying the catalog provider, Gravitino will
            use the type as the provider to create the managed catalog. If the catalog type does
            not support managed catalog, users need to specify the provider to create the catalog.

        *property* type\_name[¶](#gravitino.dto.catalog_dto.CatalogDTO.Type.type_name "Permalink to this definition")
        :   The name of the catalog type.

# gravitino.api.job.job\_template\_change.JobTemplateChange[¶](#gravitino-api-job-job-template-change-jobtemplatechange "Permalink to this heading")

*class* gravitino.api.job.job\_template\_change.JobTemplateChange[¶](#gravitino.api.job.job_template_change.JobTemplateChange "Permalink to this definition")
:   Bases: `object`

    The interface for job template changes. A job template change is an operation that modifies a job
    template. It can be one of the following:

    > * Rename the job template.
    > * Update the comment of the job template.
    > * Update the job template details, such as executable, arguments, environments, custom
    >   fields, etc.

        :   True if the schema exists and is dropped successfully, false otherwise.

        Raises:
        :   NonEmptySchemaException: If the schema is not empty and cascade is false.

    :   List schemas under the entity.

        If an entity such as a table, view exists, its parent schemas must also exist and must be
        returned by this discovery method. For example, if table a.b.t exists, this method invoked as
        listSchemas(a) must return [b] in the result array

        Raises:
        :   NoSuchCatalogException: If the catalog does not exist.

        Returns:
        :   A list of schema names under the namespace.

:   Bases: [`ColumnChange`](gravitino.api.rel.table_change.TableChange.html#gravitino.api.rel.table_change.TableChange.ColumnChange "gravitino.api.rel.table_change.TableChange.ColumnChange")

    A TableChange to add a field.

    The implementation may need to back-fill all the existing data to add this new column,
    or remember the column default value specified here and let the reader fill the column value
    when reading existing data that do not have this new column.

    If the field already exists, the change must result in an IllegalArgumentException.
    If the new field is nested and its parent does not exist or is not a struct, the change must
    result in an IllegalArgumentException.

# gravitino.api.job.job\_template.JobTemplate[¶](#gravitino-api-job-job-template-jobtemplate "Permalink to this heading")

*class* gravitino.api.job.job\_template.JobTemplate(*builder: [BaseBuilder](#gravitino.api.job.job_template.JobTemplate.BaseBuilder "gravitino.api.job.job_template.JobTemplate.BaseBuilder")*)[¶](#gravitino.api.job.job_template.JobTemplate "Permalink to this definition")
:   Bases: `ABC`

    JobTemplate is a class to define all the configuration parameters for a job.

    JobType is enum to define the type of the job, because Gravitino needs different runtime
    environments to execute different types of jobs, so the job type is required.

    Some parameters can be templated, which means that they can be replaced with actual values
    when running the job, for example, arguments can be { “{input\_path}}”, “{{output\_path}” },
    environment variables can be { “foo”: “{{foo\_value}}”, “bar”: “{{bar\_value}}” }. the parameters
    support templating are: arguments, environments.

    \_\_init\_\_(*builder: [BaseBuilder](#gravitino.api.job.job_template.JobTemplate.BaseBuilder "gravitino.api.job.job_template.JobTemplate.BaseBuilder")*)[¶](#gravitino.api.job.job_template.JobTemplate.__init__ "Permalink to this definition")

    Gravitino Metalake is the top-level metadata repository for users. It contains a list of catalogs
    as sub-level metadata collections. With GravitinoMetalake, users can list, create, load,
    alter and drop a catalog with specified identifier.

            provides a managed implementation. Currently, the model and fileset catalog support
            None provider. For the details, please refer to the Catalog.Type.

            properties: The properties of the catalog.

    delete\_job\_template(*job\_template\_name: str*) → bool[¶](#gravitino.client.gravitino_metalake.GravitinoMetalake.delete_job_template "Permalink to this definition")
    :   Deletes a job template by its name. This will remove the job template from Gravitino, and it
        will no longer be available for execution. Only when all the jobs associated with this job
        template are completed, failed or cancelled, the job template can be deleted successfully,
        otherwise it will throw InUseException. Returns false if the job template to be deleted does
        not exist.

        The deletion of a job template will also delete all the jobs associated with this template.

        Args:
        :   job\_template\_name: The name of the job template to delete.

        Returns:
        :   bool: True if the job template was deleted successfully, False if the job template
            does not exist.

        Raises:
        :   InUseException: If the job template is currently in use by any jobs, it cannot be deleted.

    | [`PROPERTY_DEFAULT_URI_NAME`](#gravitino.client.generic_model_version.GenericModelVersion.PROPERTY_DEFAULT_URI_NAME "gravitino.client.generic_model_version.GenericModelVersion.PROPERTY_DEFAULT_URI_NAME") | The property name for the default URI name of the model version. |
    | [`URI_NAME_UNKNOWN`](#gravitino.client.generic_model_version.GenericModelVersion.URI_NAME_UNKNOWN "gravitino.client.generic_model_version.GenericModelVersion.URI_NAME_UNKNOWN") | The reserved URI name to indicate the URI name is unknown. |

    PROPERTY\_DEFAULT\_URI\_NAME *= 'default-uri-name'*[¶](#gravitino.client.generic_model_version.GenericModelVersion.PROPERTY_DEFAULT_URI_NAME "Permalink to this definition")
    :   The property name for the default URI name of the model version.

    URI\_NAME\_UNKNOWN *= 'unknown'*[¶](#gravitino.client.generic_model_version.GenericModelVersion.URI_NAME_UNKNOWN "Permalink to this definition")
    :   The reserved URI name to indicate the URI name is unknown.

    aliases() → List[str][¶](#gravitino.client.generic_model_version.GenericModelVersion.aliases "Permalink to this definition")
    :   The aliases of this model version. The aliases are the alternative names of the model version.
        The aliases are optional. The aliases are unique for a model version. If the alias is already
        set to one model version, it cannot be set to another model version.

        Returns:
        :   The aliases of the model version.

    comment() → str | None[¶](#gravitino.client.generic_model_version.GenericModelVersion.comment "Permalink to this definition")
    :   The comment of this model version. This comment can be different from the comment of the model
        to provide more detailed information about this version.

        Returns:
        :   The comment of the model version. None is returned if no comment is set.

    properties() → Dict[str, str][¶](#gravitino.client.generic_model_version.GenericModelVersion.properties "Permalink to this definition")
    :   The properties of the model version. The properties are key-value pairs that can be used to
        store additional information of the model version. The properties are optional.

        Returns:
        :   The properties of the model version. An empty dictionary is returned if no properties are set.

    uri() → str[¶](#gravitino.client.generic_model_version.GenericModelVersion.uri "Permalink to this definition")
    :   The unnamed URI of the model artifact. The URI is the location of the model artifact. The URI can be a
        file path or a remote URI.

        Returns:
        :   The URI of the model artifact.

    uris() → Dict[str, str][¶](#gravitino.client.generic_model_version.GenericModelVersion.uris "Permalink to this definition")
    :   The name and corresponding URI of the model artifact. The key is the name of the URI, and the
        value is the location of the model artifact, which can be a file path or a remote URI.

        The “unknown” URI name is reserved for the compatibility with single URI.

        Returns:
        :   The URIs of the model version, the key is the name of the URI and the value is the URI of
            the model artifact.

    version() → int[¶](#gravitino.client.generic_model_version.GenericModelVersion.version "Permalink to this definition")
    :   The version of this model object. The version number is an integer number starts from 0. Each
        time the model checkpoint / snapshot is linked to the registered, the version number will be
        increased by 1.

        Returns:
        :   The version of the model object.

# gravitino.api.catalog\_change.CatalogChange[¶](#gravitino-api-catalog-change-catalogchange "Permalink to this heading")

*class* gravitino.api.catalog\_change.CatalogChange[¶](#gravitino.api.catalog_change.CatalogChange "Permalink to this definition")
:   Bases: `ABC`

    A catalog change is a change to a catalog. It can be used to rename a catalog, update the comment
    of a catalog, set a property and value pair for a catalog, or remove a property from a catalog.

:   Bases: `DataClassJsonMixin`

    A name identifier is a sequence of names separated by dots. It’s used to identify a metalake, a
    catalog, a schema or a table. For example, “metalake1” can represent a metalake,
    “metalake1.catalog1” can represent a catalog, “metalake1.catalog1.schema1” can represent a
    schema.

    :   Retrieves a List of Credential objects.

        Returns:
        :   A List of Credential objects. In most cases the array only contains

        one credential. If the object like Fileset contains multiple locations
        for different storages like HDFS, S3, the array will contain multiple
        credentials. The array could be empty if you request a credential for
        a catalog but the credential provider couldn’t generate the credential
        for the catalog, like S3 token credential provider only generate
        credential for the specific object like Fileset,Table. There will be at
        most one credential for one credential type.

    | [`PROPERTY_PACKAGE`](#gravitino.client.generic_model_catalog.GenericModelCatalog.PROPERTY_PACKAGE "gravitino.client.generic_model_catalog.GenericModelCatalog.PROPERTY_PACKAGE") | A reserved property to specify the package location of the catalog. |
    | `rest_client` |  |

    PROPERTY\_PACKAGE *= 'package'*[¶](#gravitino.client.generic_model_catalog.GenericModelCatalog.PROPERTY_PACKAGE "Permalink to this definition")
    :   A reserved property to specify the package location of the catalog. The “package” is a string
        of path to the folder where all the catalog related dependencies is located. The dependencies
        under the “package” will be loaded by Gravitino to create the catalog.

        The property “package” is not needed if the catalog is a built-in one, Gravitino will search
        the proper location using “provider” to load the dependencies. Only when the folder is in
        different location, the “package” property is needed.

    *class* Type(*value*)[¶](#gravitino.client.generic_model_catalog.GenericModelCatalog.Type "Permalink to this definition")
    :   Bases: `Enum`

        The type of the catalog.

        FILESET *= ('fileset', True)*[¶](#gravitino.client.generic_model_catalog.GenericModelCatalog.Type.FILESET "Permalink to this definition")
        :   Catalog Type for Fileset System (including HDFS, S3, etc.), like path/to/file

        MESSAGING *= ('messaging', False)*[¶](#gravitino.client.generic_model_catalog.GenericModelCatalog.Type.MESSAGING "Permalink to this definition")
        :   Catalog Type for Message Queue, like kafka://topic

        MODEL *= ('model', True)*[¶](#gravitino.client.generic_model_catalog.GenericModelCatalog.Type.MODEL "Permalink to this definition")
        :   Catalog Type for ML model

        RELATIONAL *= ('relational', False)*[¶](#gravitino.client.generic_model_catalog.GenericModelCatalog.Type.RELATIONAL "Permalink to this definition")
        :   “Catalog Type for Relational Data Structure, like db.table, catalog.db.table.

        UNSUPPORTED *= ('unsupported', False)*[¶](#gravitino.client.generic_model_catalog.GenericModelCatalog.Type.UNSUPPORTED "Permalink to this definition")
        :   Catalog Type for test only.

        *property* supports\_managed\_catalog[¶](#gravitino.client.generic_model_catalog.GenericModelCatalog.Type.supports_managed_catalog "Permalink to this definition")
        :   A flag to indicate if the catalog type supports managed catalog. Managed catalog is a
            concept in Gravitino, which means Gravitino will manage the lifecycle of the catalog
            and its subsidiaries. If the catalog type supports managed catalog, users can create
            managed catalog of this type without specifying the catalog provider, Gravitino will
            use the type as the provider to create the managed catalog. If the catalog type does
            not support managed catalog, users need to specify the provider to create the catalog.

        *property* type\_name[¶](#gravitino.client.generic_model_catalog.GenericModelCatalog.Type.type_name "Permalink to this definition")
        :   The name of the catalog type.

    link\_model\_version(*model\_ident: [NameIdentifier](gravitino.name_identifier.NameIdentifier.html#gravitino.name_identifier.NameIdentifier "gravitino.name_identifier.NameIdentifier")*, *uri: str*, *aliases: List[str]*, *comment: str*, *properties: Dict[str, str]*) → None[¶](#gravitino.client.generic_model_catalog.GenericModelCatalog.link_model_version "Permalink to this definition")
    :   Link a new model version to the registered model object. The new model version will be
        added to the model object. If the model object does not exist, it will throw an
        exception. If the version alias already exists in the model, it will throw an exception.

        Args:
        :   model\_ident: The identifier of the model.
            uri: The URI of the model version.
            aliases: The aliases of the model version. The aliases of the model version. The
            aliases should be unique in this model, otherwise the
            ModelVersionAliasesAlreadyExistException will be thrown. The aliases are optional and
            can be empty.
            comment: The comment of the model version.
            properties: The properties of the model version.

        Raises:
        :   NoSuchModelException: If the model does not exist.
            ModelVersionAliasesAlreadyExistException: If the aliases of the model version already exist.

        :   model\_ident: The identifier of the model.

            aliases should be unique in this model, otherwise the
            ModelVersionAliasesAlreadyExistException will be thrown. The aliases are optional and
            can be empty.
            comment: The comment of the model version.
            properties: The properties of the model version.

        Raises:
        :   NoSuchModelException: If the model does not exist.
            ModelVersionAliasesAlreadyExistException: If the aliases of the model version already exist.

# gravitino.filesystem.gvfs\_hook.GravitinoVirtualFileSystemHook[¶](#gravitino-filesystem-gvfs-hook-gravitinovirtualfilesystemhook "Permalink to this heading")

*class* gravitino.filesystem.gvfs\_hook.GravitinoVirtualFileSystemHook[¶](#gravitino.filesystem.gvfs_hook.GravitinoVirtualFileSystemHook "Permalink to this definition")
:   Bases: `ABC`

    Represents a hook that can be used to intercept file system operations. The implementor
    should handle the exception, if any, in the pre-hook method, otherwise the exception will be
    thrown to the caller and fail the operation. Besides, the implemented pre-hook method should
    be lightweight and fast, otherwise it will slow down the operation. The pre-hook method may
    be called more than once and in parallel, so the implementor should handle the concurrent and
    idempotent issues if required.

    \_\_init\_\_()[¶](#gravitino.filesystem.gvfs_hook.GravitinoVirtualFileSystemHook.__init__ "Permalink to this definition")

    Methods

    | --- | --- |

    :   Retrieves a List of Credential objects.

        Returns:
        :   A List of Credential objects. In most cases the array only contains

        one credential. If the object like Fileset contains multiple locations
        for different storages like HDFS, S3, the array will contain multiple
        credentials. The array could be empty if you request a credential for
        a catalog but the credential provider couldn’t generate the credential
        for the catalog, like S3 token credential provider only generate
        credential for the specific object like Fileset,Table. There will be at
        most one credential for one credential type.
